title: What If Every Freshwater Mussel Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every freshwater mussel vanished? Rivers would lose their quiet cleaners.
One mussel can filter roughly 15 to 20 gallons of water every single day.
They pull out algae, sediment and bacteria, and they lock away carbon, phosphorus and heavy metals.
Otters, raccoons, herons and some fish eat them, so those hunters would lose a meal.
Some species live over a century, so they can't bounce back fast.
North America already lost about 38 of its roughly 300 species, and many more are imperiled.
